In game, DayZDiag 1.29.163709, 2026-10-03, SecretRock test 5, runs 4c41175e and 312bacda (mods @SecretRock_RH, @SecretRock_RHTest, @LFHeliCore, @LFHeli_OH1): a Land_LF_RocaHeli spawned from the console (bridge command id 93) at x 13260.30, y 6.00, 0.3 m from the registered one horizontally and 0.22 m higher (0.37 m apart, inside the 0.75 m radius), created its parts (run1 server log L1:310-314) and was deleted by the next bridge command (id 94, ok; no log line names it, the deletion and the after-hash are recorded in README section 6); placed.json kept its SHA-256 (a65ff4ec31ae8603..., before and after) and the registered rock was restored with its state after an orderly restart (run2 server log L2:27). The rule that an id two entries share identifies neither comes from the cross-family review's premise note (EnsureEntryIds fills blanks without rejecting duplicates, SecretRock_Persistence.c:128-145; FindIndexById returns the first match, :148-159), not from a test. The failure itself (a neighbour's entry deleted) was derived from the code and not reproduced in game. The degraded case (ids assigned in memory whose save failed, so a deleted rock comes back after a restart) is from the review of the fix's delta (dzr9_delta.md). Sources: SecretRock_dev/reviews/2026-10-03-roca-r73/README.md sections 5 and 6, dzr9_codex.md, dzr9_delta.md, dzr9_fix.diff, prueba5/.

Vanilla 1.29 scripts: CGame.GetObjectsAtPosition3D(vector pos, float radius, out array<Object> objects, out array<CargoBase> proxyCargos) is documented as 'Returns list of all objects in sphere radius around position pos', with no order (3_game/global/game.c:924-929). SecretRock audit DZ-R9 F3, 2026-10-03, read in the code: FindExisting returned the first unclaimed Building of the persisted class within MATCH_M 0.75 m (SecretRock_Persistence.c:323), so two rocks of one class inside the radius could take each other's id and state; RestoreAll runs it at mission start and again in a pass 2 s later (CallLater in CALL_CATEGORY_SYSTEM). Fix in the mod: the rock already bound to the entry's id, else the nearest rock not yet claimed in the pass (SecretRock_Persistence.c:317, called at :395). The review of the fix (dzr9_delta.md) notes that this greedy fallback can still swap two entries when ids were regenerated after a failed save. The id lives in a script member (m_SecretRockPersistId, BindId and IdOf at SecretRock_Persistence.c:112-126), so no rock carries it across a restart. Cross-family review of the restore (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, read-only), six rounds on 2026-10-03, one on each restore rule the section gave in PRs #97 and #99, traced every one into an entry that takes the wrong entity or gets a second one. #97 round 1, through the fixed code (blob ac8b38ef), R21-01: an entry left in the file by an unregister whose save failed (Save's result ignored, SecretRock_Persistence.c:263) takes the nearest unclaimed rock even though it carries another entry's id, rebinds it and applies its own state (:335-346, :395-421). #97 round 2, R21-03: the same stale entry takes an admin's console rock that carries no id; R21-04: an entry whose id was regenerated after a failed save would get a second rock under a rule that excludes every entity with another id (:547-551, :407-417; MissionServer.c:9-10 schedules the second pass). Post-merge review of #97 (on f42f503), R21-05: the merged rule created an entity whenever the radius held none of the class, which a traced scenario turns into two entities (an id regenerated after a failed save, then the entity moved out of the radius), and the same branch creates a second entity for an entity outside the radius, under another class name (SecretRock normalises Land_LF_RocaHeli_Down at SecretRock_Persistence.c:74-77 and compares the normalised class at :330) or not yet loaded by the engine. #99 round 1 (on 6be8785), R21-06: a list of the restore's own creations kept per mission and cleared at its end misses the previous mission's entities if they still live; R21-07: two loaded entities carrying one id let the second take over the binding. #99 round 2 (on 4e30ee7), R21-08: a list of every live entity kept by EEInit and EEDelete misses a creation in flight, which joins it from its EEInit before it carries the id (SecretRock creates at :407 and binds at :417), so a pass started from that EEInit creates a second one. #99 round 3 (on 5b572e4), R21-09: a reservation of the entry during the creation does not stop a pass that reloads the registry and gets a new copy of the entry without the reservation (each load builds a new SecretRock_PlacedFile, TryLoadPath at SecretRock_Persistence.c:496-498, read by RestoreAll at :367); R21-10: a creation that returns no entity (:408) leaves the entry reserved for good, a liveness defect that neither binds a wrong entity nor creates a second one. Round 3 also notes that SecretRock starts no restore pass from EEInit (RestoreAll is called only from SecretRock_MissionServer.c:31), so R21-08 and R21-09 are counterexamples to the rules' text, not failures observed in the mod. All are traces through the code and the rules' text; none was reproduced in game. The section therefore gives no restore rule: point 2 keeps the documented absence of order and that a position match proves nothing, and lists these failures as an open problem with no automatic rule reviewed sound.

Vanilla 1.29 scripts: ScriptCallQueue.Remove(func fn), 'remove specific call from queue' (2_gamelib/tools.c:65); CGame.GetCallQueue documents CALL_CATEGORY_SYSTEM as 'calls & timers in this queue are processed every time without any restrictions' (3_game/global/game.c:1515); EntityAI.EEDelete is 'Called right before object deleting' (3_game/entities/entityai.c:933-934). SecretRock audit DZ-R9 F6, 2026-10-03, read in the code: MissionServer.OnMissionFinish set the shutdown flag (SecretRock_MissionServer.c:13) while RestoreAll set it back to false on every restore (SecretRock_Persistence.c:350), so a restore pass still queued in CALL_CATEGORY_SYSTEM (2 s after start, or a retry) could reopen saving before the world's entities were deleted, and their EEDelete calls would then unregister entries. Fix in the mod: OnMissionFinish removes SecretRock_RestorePlaced from the queue before setting the flag (SecretRock_MissionServer.c:15-20); the review of the fix's delta found no new loss path. The real shutdown order in game was not confirmed. Sources: SecretRock_dev/reviews/2026-10-03-roca-r73/README.md section 5, dzr9_codex.md, dzr9_delta.md, dzr9_fix.diff.

In game, DayZ 1.30.164014 Exp, LFSkateboard R1e, 2026-10-07, as pipeline inbox fb-20261007-010022-0cee reports it (project LFSkateboard): a roll loop built by hand to reach AbstractWave.SetFrequency (SoundParams, SoundObjectBuilder.AddEnvSoundVariables, BuildSoundObject, SetKind(WAVEEFFECTEX), SetParent on the player, GetSoundScene().Play3D) played, its header loaded and logged, but was barely audible, while one-shots of the same character sound bases played through PlaySoundSet were loud. Not re-measured for this change.
